title: FPT Corporation and Niels Bohr Institute Partner to Advance Quantum Research and Talent Development in Vietnam and Denmark - Quantum Computing Report
gist: Vietnam's FPT Corporation (HOSE: FPT) signed an MoU with the Niels Bohr Institute in Copenhagen for joint quantum research, PhD and faculty exchanges, and workshops, formalized at the Vietnam-Denmark Business Forum attended by President Tô Lâm and King Frederik X. FPT aims to plug its 44,000-strong engineering workforce into Denmark's DKK 1.5B Novo Nordisk Foundation program targeting a fault-tolerant quantum computer by 2034.

insights.claim: FPT Corporation and the Niels Bohr Institute at the University of Copenhagen signed an MoU covering joint quantum research programs, academic exchanges for doctoral researchers, faculty and technical specialists, and joint scientific workshops.
insights.speaker: Mohamed Abdel-Kareem
insights.so_what: Talent-and-research MoU, non-binding; minimal near-term financial impact for FPT.
insights.locator: Under the framework, FPT and NBI

insights.claim: The MoU was exchanged by Pham Minh Tuan, EVP of FPT and CEO of FPT Software, and Prof. Joachim Mathiesen, Director of NBI.
insights.speaker: Mohamed Abdel-Kareem
insights.so_what: Senior-level sponsorship at FPT Software suggests quantum is part of its strategic narrative.

insights.claim: The partnership expands FPT's Nordic operations in Kongens Lyngby, Denmark, into deep-tech quantum information science.
insights.speaker: Mohamed Abdel-Kareem
insights.so_what: FPT is using European footprint to move up the value chain from IT outsourcing.

themes.theme: FPT strategy: workforce into hybrid quantum services

insights.claim: FPT seeks to position its 44,000-strong engineering workforce to deploy hybrid classical-quantum solutions across manufacturing, healthcare and enterprise software by aligning with the Niels Bohr Institute.
insights.speaker: Mohamed Abdel-Kareem
insights.so_what: IT services firms see quantum as a future consulting/integration line; watch for FPT quantum service revenue disclosures.
insights.quote: FPT seeks to position its 44,000-strong engineering workforce to deploy hybrid classical-quantum solutions

insights.claim: The deal is meant to accelerate Vietnam's national quantum computing roadmap by connecting domestic tech talent with European quantum research infrastructure, amid rising Southeast Asian efforts to build quantum software, algorithm and hardware-maintenance capabilities.
insights.speaker: Mohamed Abdel-Kareem
insights.so_what: Southeast Asia is entering quantum via talent and software, not hardware.

insights.claim: The Niels Bohr Institute anchors Denmark's national ambition to build a universal fault-tolerant quantum computer by 2034, backed by a DKK 1.5B Novo Nordisk Foundation quantum computing program.
insights.speaker: Mohamed Abdel-Kareem
insights.so_what: Denmark's foundation-funded program is a major European quantum capital pool with a 2034 fault-tolerance target.
insights.quote: Denmark’s national ambition to develop a universal fault-tolerant quantum computer by 2034
insights.locator: By aligning with the Niels Bohr Institute

insights.claim: The MoU was formalized at the Vietnam-Denmark Business Forum in Copenhagen in the presence of Vietnamese President Tô Lâm and King Frederik X, and supports the bilateral Comprehensive Strategic Partnership set during the State visit.
insights.speaker: Mohamed Abdel-Kareem
insights.so_what: Quantum is being folded into state-level tech diplomacy between smaller economies.
